narrative: For rounds 1-8 the agent pushed CI-iteration commits (Dockerfile, goreleaser v2, CGO flags, chown) without answering round 0, so Copilot re-raised the same ~15 findings every round and all 62 threads were answered at once at 04:23 with pasted templates; two of those replies (F4, F55) described an unrelated fix. The big fix commit efcabf1 split the version string (.Tag for ldflags, .Version for archives) instead of unifying it as F6 asked. That left v-prefixed mkmanifest fixtures and docs (round 9) and kept the `baseURL/ver/filename` 404, which the agent waved off twice (F66, F70/F74) before conceding it at F79. Later rounds were mostly drift from incomplete sweeps (docs missing -tag, stale v0.1.0 literals, readlink after seq) plus a long tail of speculative hardening (path traversal, HOME unset, whitespace flags) that the agent accepted every time.
guidance_observations: Reply to and fix open findings before pushing more commits; each unrelated CI push re-triggered a review that re-raised the same unaddressed findings, which accounts for rounds 1-8.
A reply template pasted across many threads must be checked per thread against the named commit's diff; two threads were marked addressed by a reply describing a different change.
A value-shape decision (v-prefixed vs v-stripped) needed one grep for the old literal across code, tests, docs and both producers; skipping that sweep fed rounds 9, 11, 12, 14 and 22.

When a reviewer argues one parameter serves two contracts, the agent should test each contract concretely instead of reasoning that changing a third site made them equal; that error cost two extra rounds on the URL bug.

From round 19 on the agent stopped replying per thread and fixed findings it believed were 'suppressed' straight from commit messages; the threads were found only at the merge gate, so replies lagged fixes by up to 50 minutes.
